plan text.why: EXPLAIN prints Pondra's plan, made with rules and scans of its own (optimize.rs, scan.rs): the text differs where the answers agree

a write explained.why: EXPLAIN of an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or COPY: Pondra's writes aren't DataFusion's plans

the runner's own.why: a table or function DataFusion's runner makes in Rust before the file runs (range_partitioned, table_with_metadata, union_table, async_abs, …): no SQL in the file makes it

the node's memory.why: datafusion.runtime.* (memory limit, spill folder, caches) is the node's, set as it starts (PONDRA_MEMORY_MB, PONDRA_SPILL_DIR), not a session's

microseconds.why: a table's TIMESTAMP keeps microseconds, as Postgres, Delta and Iceberg do; DataFusion's keeps nanoseconds, which the answer shows

an order not asked for.why: the same rows in another order, from a query with no ORDER BY: SQL leaves the order open, and Pondra's plans give another

interval arithmetic.why: `n * INTERVAL '1 hour'` and `INTERVAL … / n`, which DataFusion refuses and Pondra computes as Postgres does

FETCH FIRST.why: `FETCH FIRST | NEXT n ROWS ONLY`, standard SQL that DataFusion refuses and Pondra takes, as Postgres and DuckDB do (friendly.rs)
